solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sensible to capture pencil marking on part of avian skeleton

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it inside, so the first word surrounds what follows

parts.note: sensible means wise
HB is the grading stamped on a standard pencil (hard black)
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sensibly sketches a mark in pencil onto a bird bone in a biology class.
explanation.definitionFit: The forked bone of a bird's breast, pulled apart for luck, is a piece of the bird's skeleton.

clue.text: Saint occupying extremely religious office

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit within it, so saint goes inside the next word

parts.note: extremely means very

explanation.surface: A saint holds a post in an extremely devout office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely religious' reads as one phrase, but 'extremely' is the container and 'religious office' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is a room in a church where clergy robe and parish business is done, so a church office.

clue.text: Town near Oxford, note, toured by a major university figure

indicators.note: something toured by a group is gone round by it, so these words enclose the note

parts.note: major means big
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A senior academic tours a town close to Oxford, making a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A major university figure' reads as one person, but it splits into three pieces; Abingdon is home to an old Oxford-linked school and lies on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Abingdon is a market town in Oxfordshire a few miles south of the city of Oxford.

clue.text: A lot of dirt is ghastly

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: grime is ingrained dirt

explanation.surface: A great deal of filth is a horrible sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim and ghastly both describe something dreadful, repellent or depressing to look at.

clue.text: Comedian's mocking cry absorbing street

indicators.note: to absorb something is to take it in, so the cry surrounds the street

parts.note: a jeer is a taunting shout
ST is the address abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A comic's taunting shout takes in the whole street.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A jester was a court entertainer, so a joker or comic performer by trade.

clue.text: A Parisian brought up a couple of lines without significance

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it
L is an abbreviation for line, so two lines are LL

explanation.surface: A Parisian raises a few lines that mean nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Null describes something void or having no force or meaning, as in null and void.

clue.text: Square, popular in Tyneside area

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so popular sits within the area

parts.note: NE is north-east England, where Tyneside (around Newcastle) lies
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A town square that is popular around Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a place, but here it is a number that is the square of another: three times three.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is three multiplied by itself, which makes it a perfect square number.

clue.text: Sharp comment with indication about energy in cooking device

indicators.note: about means going round, so the comment and the indication together enclose energy

parts.note: a barb is a cutting remark
a cue is a signal or hint
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A cutting remark and a hint about energy use, made over a cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is an outdoor grill for cooking food over charcoal or gas.

clue.text: Physicist initially well-informed about light particle

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: first letter of physicist
hot on a subject means knowledgeable about it
on means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A physicist who is well up on the subject of light particles.
explanation.definitionFit: A photon is the quantum of electromagnetic radiation, the elementary particle that carries light.

clue.text: Satisfied story is missing a show of courage

parts.note: met as in met a demand, satisfied it

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the next word is taken away from the story

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A contented tale lacks any display of bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle is spirit or resilience in the face of difficulty, demonstrated when someone is put to the test.

clue.text: Last characters in church to feel godly or saintly

indicators.note: take the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Being in church makes one feel pious or saintly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'godly' looks like the definition, but its last letter is needed; 'saintly' defines after the link 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy means sacred or devoted to God, as a saint is.

clue.text: Support backing people in fierce speech

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for support is reversed

parts.note: aid means help or support
a tribe is a group of people

explanation.surface: Getting behind a group of people in a heated address.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a ranting tirade against someone.

clue.text: Confused everybody offshore?

parts.note: all means everybody
at sea means out on the water, away from the shore

explanation.surface: Is everyone out on the water muddled?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'offshore' must be read literally as AT SEA, which is also the idiom for bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all at sea is an idiom for being completely bewildered or lost.

clue.text: One moving into residence after aristocrat kept up great friendliness

indicators.note: the residence part comes after the aristocrat part
in a down clue, kept up means held upright, so read from the bottom

parts.note: a nob is an informal word for a toff or aristocrat

indicators.note: one moving into a place goes inside it

parts.note: a home is a residence
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone moves house after a lord is kept on, in a spirit of goodwill.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is cheerful good nature and geniality towards others.

clue.text: Rector's first boy brought in some bells for his own use?

indicators.note: brought in means put inside, so the bells surround what goes before

parts.note: a peal is a set of bells or their ringing

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of rector
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A rector's son is brought in to ring the church bells for his own amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal belongings are things belonging to one individual, kept for private use.

clue.text: Observe article that makes you show anger

parts.note: to observe is to see
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Watching a certain item makes you furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to be inwardly furious, boiling with rage.

clue.text: Good individual no longer with us

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A good person has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone is a euphemism for dead, someone who has departed this life.

clue.text: Stringed instrument mostly good for Scottish sailor

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: guid is the Scots word for good
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is mostly fine for a sailor from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish' looks like it describes the sailor, but it tells you to use the Scots form of good.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitar is a fretted instrument played by plucking or strumming its strings.

clue.text: A thing about boarding old British plane

indicators.note: boarding a plane means getting into it, so about goes inside

parts.note: a jet is a plane
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Something to do with getting onto an old British aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An object is any material item, an article or entity one can see or touch.

clue.text: Partiality shown by arts graduates around India

indicators.note: the graduates go around India, enclosing it

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, so two or more are BAS
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Favouritism displayed by humanities graduates travelling round India.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is a prejudice that favours one side, so a leaning or partiality.

clue.text: Some optimism returns after reflecting for a period

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters are read backwards
some of a phrase means only part of its letters are used

explanation.surface: Some optimism comes back after a spell of thinking things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' looks like the reversal signal, but it holds the letters; 'reflecting' turns MRET round.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a fixed span of time, such as a school term or a term of office.

clue.text: Maker of uniforms possibly to follow common soldiers

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A uniform maker may follow the ordinary troops around.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor cuts and sews clothes to measure, uniforms being one example of such work.

clue.text: Declining to accept sources of any really hoary old theatre piece?

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the worse word holds the initials

parts.note: worse describes something declining in quality

indicators.note: sources are origins, so the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A tired old stage production, getting worse and really hoary.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is figurative: a warhorse is a familiar, much-performed play or piece that keeps being revived.
explanation.definitionFit: A warhorse is a hackneyed work staged over and over, so a stale old theatrical standard.

clue.text: Something to revolve around a half-dozen turns

indicators.note: a word that turns round is read backwards

parts.note: half a dozen is six

explanation.surface: A pivot spun six times.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is the line about which a body rotates, like the Earth's spin.
